body:
I created a PR with the changes; please take a look. I have also started working on the PR points.

https://github.com/whatwg/html/pull/12424

A slight refinement from my initial post to clarify the exact intended behavior for implementers:

**Affected controls**

fieldset readonly would propagate to:

- input elements in states that support readonly (text, email, number, date, etc.)
- textarea elements
- Form-associated custom elements (via a new formReadonlyCallback, parallel to formDisabledCallback)

It would not affect: 
input[type=checkbox], input[type=radio], input[type=button], select, button — the same controls for which readonly is meaningless.

Today you have to do this:

```
<fieldset>
  <input type="text" name="name" value="Ada Lovelace" readonly>
  <textarea name="notes" readonly>Leave at door.</textarea>
  <input type="checkbox" name="confirm"> <!-- no readonly needed -->
</fieldset>
```

With this proposal:

```
<fieldset readonly>
  <input type="text" name="name" value="Ada Lovelace">
  <textarea name="notes">Leave at door.</textarea>
  <input type="checkbox" name="confirm"> <!-- unaffected, as expected -->
</fieldset>
```

**Nesting**

Nesting follows the same rules as disabled: a readonly fieldset inside another readonly fieldset propagates correctly, with the same legend child exclusion.

**Form-associated custom elements**

A formReadonlyCallback(readOnly: boolean) would be added parallel to [formDisabledCallback](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/custom-elements.html#custom-element-reactions), allowing custom elements to react when their readonly state changes due to an ancestor fieldset.

**Symmetry with disabled**

The spec change would mirror the existing fieldset disabled definition precisely, with the addition of the "supports readonly" qualifier since not all controls have a meaningful read-only state.
Can you clarify in which situations this feature would be useful? Just "parity with `disabled`" is not sufficient I think.

Hi @zcorpan,

My specific use case for requesting this feature stems from developing an enterprise web component library. To effectively use native forms with web components, we need to support a crucial form control requirement: the ability to put an entire form—including all its web components into a read-only or disabled mode.

While this might not be a common use case for everyone / web where not all form controls support readonly (altrough it has use cases - see end of post), it has been a strict requirement for a lot of enterprise component libraries I have ever worked on or worked with.
https://www.oracle.com/webfolder/technetwork/jet/jsdocs/oj.ojFormLayout.html#readonly for example

While supporting this natively on a standard webpage without web components is a nice feature, most component libraries allow developers to transform web components even a custom select dropdown into a read-only mode.
 
Being able to do this natively without having to code a custom form manager using form-associated, similar to how disabled works would be a huge selling point for writing native forms saving on custom reactivity handling. 
It allows developers to leverage native state propagation instead of relying on a framework or implementing it themselves.


**Few use cases:**
- Review Your Details / Multi-Step Confirmation Screen
- Inline View / Edit toggle for forms - by default you view a Client or Product / Order and you want to switch to the Edit mode
- The readonly mode is also often used for performance and developer ergonomics - instead of having an edit and view component an readonly property is set to render the value with the correct view formatter - this is probably the most common use case and it's often used as part of a group / form.

Disabled styling reduces color contrast, making text difficult to read for low-vision users who simply need to review their entered data on a confirmation screeny, and more importantly, disabled fields are omitted from native form submission while readonly form fields are not.

The most important feature is to support 'formReadonlyCallback' in order to use it in web components as it's already done in disabled:
_If element is [disabled](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-fe-disabled), then [enqueue a custom element callback reaction](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#enqueue-a-custom-element-callback-reaction) with element, callback name "formDisabledCallback", and « true »._
REF: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-fe-disabled
